suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-7 adds this relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. Hemodynamically established precapillary pulmonary hypertension can occur with myeloproliferative neoplasms; in polycythemia vera the registry evidence is strongest for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension, while group-5 PH is also represented across the MPN cohort. Require confirmed polycythemia vera and separately established precapillary pulmonary hypertension using appropriate hemodynamic evaluation, with classification of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension versus group-5 PH when applicable. The source is strongest for CTEPH in polycythemia vera/essential thrombocythemia and does not support postcapillary pulmonary hypertension caused by left-heart disease. Do not infer pulmonary hypertension from polycythemia vera, dyspnea, hypoxemia, or an isolated echocardiographic estimate alone. Treat the registry as population-level complication evidence rather than automatic individual causation. Preserve left-heart disease, chronic lung disease or hypoxia, sleep-disordered breathing, unrelated thromboembolic disease, medications, and other recognized pulmonary-hypertension causes. The cited literature supports only this constrained relationship and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
